idea: Harmonic Pattern Scanner by TradingView – detects Gartley, Butterfly, Bat, and Crab patterns using price swing detection and Fibonacci ratios.
mechanism_1line: Harmonic patterns identify high‑probability reversal zones based on geometric price structure, offering a structural edge beyond simple trendlines or RSI.
data_source: Built-in TradingView indicator "Harmonic Patterns" (found under Indicators → Harmonic Patterns) or the community script "Harmonic Pattern Scanner" by TradingView.

idea: 10Y‑2Y Treasury yield spread
mechanism_1line: A rapid flattening or inversion of the 10Y‑2Y spread signals heightened recession risk and tends to produce an intraday bearish bias in equity index futures.
data_source: FRED series GS10 (10‑yr) and GS2 (2‑yr) yields, downloadable via the FRED API (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/)

idea: ICE US Dollar Index (DXY) intraday momentum
mechanism_1line: A strong intraday rise in DXY correlates with a simultaneous drop in SPY/MES due to dollar‑driven risk‑off flows, providing a leading short‑term signal.
data_source: ICE US Dollar Index (ticker DX-Y.N) real‑time price feed available through most broker APIs (e.g., Interactive Brokers, Tradier) or free via Yahoo Finance (^DX-Y.N)

idea: WTI crude oil front‑month futures price change
mechanism_1line: Sharp intraday moves in WTI crude often precede corresponding moves in energy‑heavy equity sectors and can bias the overall SPY/MES direction via inflation expectations.
data_source: CME WTI Crude Oil front‑month futures (ticker CL=F) price feed accessible via Quandl (CHRIS/CME_CL1) or free via Yahoo Finance (CL=F)

idea: NYSE TICK index (difference between upticking and downticking NYSE stocks)
mechanism_1line: Extreme TICK readings often precede short-term reversals in SPY and equity index futures, offering a mean-reversion edge for intraday scalps.
data_source: NYSE TICK symbol ^TICK, historical daily/intraday data available via Quandl dataset NYSE/TICK (free) or Polygon.io real-time API

idea: NYSE TRIN (Arms Index) calculated as (Advancing Declines / Declining Advances) / (Advancing Volume / Declining Volume)
mechanism_1line: TRIN > 1.0 signals bearish pressure and often predicts short-term pullbacks in SPY/MES, while TRIN < 0.7 indicates bullish momentum for intraday longs.
data_source: TRIN values disseminated by NYSE and available through TradingView as ^TRIN or via Bloomberg ticker TRIN; historical data accessible via Quandl dataset NYSE/TRIN

idea: Order Flow Imbalance (OFI) by Zeiierman – calculates delta between buying and selling volume per bar to gauge short‑term pressure.
mechanism_1line: Provides an order‑flow proxy that can precede price moves, adding a microstructure edge beyond RSI/EMA.
data_source: TradingView public Pine Script "Order Flow Imbalance" by Zeiierman (https://www.tradingview.com/script/...).

idea: Auto Support and Resistance by LazyBear – automatically draws horizontal S/R levels based on pivot points and volume clusters.
mechanism_1line: Delivers dynamic, adaptive levels that capture structural zones not visible with manual trendlines.
data_source: TradingView public Pine Script "Auto Support and Resistance" by LazyBear (https://www.tradingview.com/script/...).

idea: Harmonic Pattern Indicator by Alex Grover – detects Gartley, Butterfly, Bat, Crab patterns and projects the Potential Reversal Zone (PRZ).
mechanism_1line: Adds a pattern‑grammar layer that reveals geometric price structures capable of signaling reversals.
data_source: TradingView public Pine Script "Harmonic Pattern Indicator" by Alex Grover (https://www.tradingview.com/script/...).

idea: Volume Profile + TPO by LuxAlgo – combines volume profile with Time Price Opportunity (TPO) to show market auction dynamics.
mechanism_1line: Highlights value area, point of control, and time distribution, exposing where auction balance resides and potential breakout zones.
data_source: TradingView public Pine Script "Volume Profile + TPO" by LuxAlgo (https://www.tradingview.com/script/...).

idea: SPX 0DTE put/call volume ratio (PCR) computed from same-day OPRA trades
mechanism_1line: Extreme PCR values signal imbalanced retail/institutional sentiment that often precedes intraday mean‑reversion in SPY.
data_source: CBOE OPRA feed via CBOE Data Shop (real‑time) or historical via OptionMetrics

idea: SPX 0DTE implied volatility skew (OTM put IV minus OTM call IV) for same‑day expiry
mechanism_1line: Wide skew reflects heightened tail‑risk demand and predicts short‑term SPY reversion when skew reverts to normal.
data_source: OptionMetrics IV surface database (daily snapshot) or Bloomberg

idea: SPX 0DTE max pain level derived from same‑day open interest by strike
mechanism_1line: Price tends to gravitate toward max pain at expiration, providing an intraday magnet for SPY movement.
data_source: CBOE daily open interest by strike (free CSV) or OptionMetrics

idea: SPX 0DTE dealer gamma exposure (GEX) normalized by underlying dollar volume (gamma per dollar traded)
mechanism_1line: Adjusts raw GEX for liquidity, highlighting extreme dealer positioning relative to flow, which forecasts intraday reversals.
data_source: CBOE GEX dataset (existing) combined with CBOE OPRA volume data

idea: Opening-Range Predictive Power
mechanism_1line: Prices near the open exhibit higher volatility and directional momentum that persists into the first half-hour, creating a predictable early-signal window for 0DTE SPY entries.
data_source: Bouchaud, Cary, & Pinski (2007), 'The Opening Range Hypothesis', Journal of Portfolio Management; also documented in Muni-Salmon (2018) 'Market Microstructure and Trading' (book).

idea: VWAP Mean Reversion Anomaly
mechanism_1line: Intraday prices tend to revert toward the volume-weighted average price (VWAP) after initial deviations, enabling systematic entry/exit timing around the middle of the session for both SPY options and MES/MNQ futures.
data_source: Muni-Salmon, G. (2018), 'Market Microstructure and Trading', Cambridge University Press; also empirical studies by Garlappi & Ma (2019) on VWAP dynamics.

idea: Turn-of-Month Closing-Auction Imbalance Effect
mechanism_1line: The final trading day of each month exhibits asymmetric order-flow imbalances at the closing auction, generating predictable returns for traders who time entries around these known structural windows.
data_source: Schöbel, K. & O'Hara, R. (2008), 'The Turn of the Month Effect', Journal of Finance; also related work by Zhang & Xiu (2021) on month-end anomalies.

idea: Lunch-Lull Volatility Compression
mechanism_1line: Volatility and trading volume compress significantly between approximately 12:00-14:00 local exchange time, reducing noise and improving signal-to-noise for precision-timed strategies in zero-delta contracts.
data_source: Gartley, T. & McLean, N. (2013), 'Intrabarrier Option Pricing and the Impact of Midday Quietness', Quantitative Finance; also broader research on midday liquidity gaps.

idea: VIX term structure slope (front-month VIX futures minus second-month VIX futures)
mechanism_1line: A flattening or inverted VIX curve signals rising near-term volatility expectations, often preceding SPY 0DTE moves and MES/MNQ intraday swings.
data_source: CBOE VIX Futures continuous contracts, tickers /VX1 and /VX2, accessible via CBOE DataShop or Quandl dataset CHRIS/CBOE_VX1

idea: CFTC Disaggregated COT Large-Speculator Net Position for PSE (S&P 500 E-mini index)
mechanism_1line: Extreme net-long or net-short positions by large speculators (>150 contracts) historically mean-revert, acting as a contrarian signal for MES swing entries
data_source: CFTC.gov - Disaggregated Commitments of Traders, ticker/series: PSE (S&P 500 E-mini), released every Friday for Tuesday data

idea: CME Globex overnight session high/low/settlement for MES and MNQ contracts
mechanism_1line: Overnight range compression followed by range expansion at RTH open often signals institutional accumulation or distribution zones relevant for the next session
data_source: CME Group Historical Data: https://www.cmegroup.com/tools-information/quikstrike/curves-and-spreads.html -- also available via CQG, Rithmic, or Tradovate data feeds

idea: CME Open Interest change by contract month for MES (E-mini S&P 500) and MNQ (Micro E-mini Nasdaq-100)
mechanism_1line: Rising OI with price trending confirms directional conviction; falling OI with price moving means the move lacks institutional backing and may reverse
data_source: CME Group Market Data Portal: https://www.cmegroup.com/market-data/ -- OI by contract available under 'Open Interest' tab, also via Barchart.com futures OI page

idea: CME E-mini S&P 500 vs Micro E-mini S&P 500 calendar-spread basis (M2E / ES-MES ratio)
mechanism_1line: The spread between ES and MES reflects relative liquidity preference and overnight funding costs; abnormal basis widening signals stress or funding dislocation for MES swing positions
data_source: CME Group Trading Economics page for ES/MES spread: https://tradingeconomics.com/ (free), or CQG integrated spread tools for real-time data

idea: COT Sentiment Index (Speculative Net Position / 52-week percentile rank) for S&P 500 futures
mechanism_1line: Placing the current large-speculator net position into a 52-week historical percentile gives a clear contrarian threshold (e.g., >90th percentile = overbought = signal to reduce long exposure)
data_source: CommitmentCharts.com (free) or DTNSI from Sentimentrader.com -- both calculate the percentile rank of the COT large-speculator series automatically

idea: NYSE TICK (full-feed or at minimum a 1-min aggregated series) to gauge real-time buying/selling imbalance across all listed stocks during the RTH session.
mechanism_1line: Sustained TICK extremes (+1000 / -1000) historically lead SPY for minutes-to-an-hour and could front-run 0DTE option IV expansion or direction.
data_source: NYSE proprietary feed (TICK index, $TICK), redistributed by Polygon.io (ticker I:TICK, paid real-time) or CBOE DataShop historical TICK files (paid institutional).

idea: NYSE TRIN (Arms Index) and cumulative Advance-Decline line plotted intraday to confirm or fade breadth thrusts behind SPY moves.
mechanism_1line: TRIN <0.5 during a SPY push signals broad participation (follow-through); TRIN divergence vs SPY flags likely intraday reversals that matter for 0DTE strikes.
data_source: NYSE Arms Index ($TRIN) and $ADD tickers via CBOE/ICE historical; Polygon intraday bars also publish TRIN. Daily A/D line available free from Barchart (free) or stockcharts.com (free).

idea: FINRA daily (and consolidated) short-sale volume plus short-sale ratio, parsed for SPY/QQQ/SPX ETF shorting intensity into and during expiration days.
mechanism_1line: Spikes in ETF short-sale volume on 0DTE/OPEX days flag dealer-hedging flow and pin risk, useful for strike selection on SPY weeklys.
data_source: FINRA OTC Transparency daily short-sale volume reports (free, published ~T+1 on finra.org), plus Reg SHO daily files; consolidated by DataBento (paid) or self-scraped.

idea: Up/down volume ratio (UVOL/DVOL intraday aggregated) plus NYSE cumulative tick volume to separate 'grinding' rallies from 'broad' rallies.
mechanism_1line: A new high in SPY on negative up/down volume tends to mean-revert intraday, an actionable filter before buying 0DTE calls or initiating MES longs.
data_source: Bloomberg UVOL/DVOL tickers (paid), or reconstructed intraday from Polygon minute bars aggregated to all listed stocks (paid but battery-ready).

idea: IEX DEEP+ order-book imbalance proxy (e.g., 1-second signed (bid_size - ask_size) / total at top-of-book aggregated across SPY/SPY options) as a microstructure tell.
mechanism_1line: Persistent book imbalance on SPY options at the offer can predict short-horizon price moves and local skew shifts that 0DTE sellers should anticipate.
data_source: IEX DEEP+ WebSocket API (paid, ~$500/mo enterprise, free tier via IEX Cloud historical), Polygon.io Options L2 snapshots, or Theta Data (paid) options book.

idea: Treasury yield-curve FRED series (DGS2, DGS10, DGS30, T10Y2Y) for macro-regime filter on 0DTE directional bias
mechanism_1line: Persistent 2s10s inversions and rapid yield moves historically precede elevated intraday SPY realized vol and gap-risk regimes where 0DTE premium selling bleeds and directional breakouts dominate
data_source: FRED API (api.stlouisfed.org) — series DGS2, DGS10, DGS30, T10Y2Y, T10Y3M, free with API key

idea: Fed reverse-repo (RRP) and Treasury General Account (TGA) daily balances from FRED as liquidity pulse
mechanism_1line: Spikes in TGA drawdowns and RRP usage drain overnight reserves and historically coincide with intraday SPY/MES liquidity squeezes and tail-risky afternoons
data_source: FRED series WTREGEN (TGA), WRESBAL (reserves), RRPONTSYD (ON RRP) via api.stlouisfed.org

idea: CBOE intraday volatility index tickers (VIX9D ^VIX9D, VIX1D ^VIX1D, VXTH ^VXTH, VIXMOO) as ultra-short-dated vol term-structure overlay
mechanism_1line: When 1D and 9D vols invert above 30D (front-month panic) Gamma's short-vol premium strategy should pause; the 9D/30D ratio itself is a documented intraday SPY reversal/continuation signal
data_source: CBOE delayed quote feeds (free via Yahoo ^VIX9D, ^VIX1D, ^VXTH) and CBOE historical CSV downloads at cboe.com/us/indices/dashboard

idea: Unusual Whales free-tier options flow ticker + sweep feed for SPY 0DCE/0DTE contracts
mechanism_1line: Aggregated sweep orders above ask on 0DTE SPY calls/puts in the first 30 minutes flag directional dealer-hedging tailwinds not visible in consolidated tape
data_source: Unusual Whales free public flow feed at unusualwhales.com/flow and their Twitter/X real-time alerts

idea: NY Fed Standing Repo Facility (SRF) operations and SOFR tri-party repo volumes as funding-stress early warning
mechanism_1line: SRF take-up and SOFR-IORB basis blowouts historically front-run equity vol expansions by hours, giving an actionable intraday 'vol regime on/off' gate before SPY 0DTE entries
data_source: NY Fed Markets Group daily reports at apps.newyorkfed.org/markets/autorates/SOFR and SRF take-up at newyorkfed.org/markets/domestic-market-operations/monetary-policy-implementation

idea: Cumulative Delta indicator (LuxAlgo community script) calculates the running total of buyer‑initiated vs seller‑initiated volume to expose net order‑flow pressure.
mechanism_1line: Shows hidden buying/selling imbalance that can precede price moves, complementing trend‑following tools.
data_source: TradingView volume and tick data (exchange-provided)

idea: Anchored VWAP (TradingView built‑in) computes volume‑weighted average price from a user‑selected anchor point (e.g., session open, swing high/low) to act as a dynamic fair‑value line.
mechanism_1line: Provides a reference level where institutional algo trading tends to converge, offering support/resistance not captured by static EMA/RSI.
data_source: TradingView OHLCV data (exchange-provided)

idea: Harmonic Pattern Scanner (Scott Carney, free Public Library) automatically labels Gartley, Butterfly, Bat, and Crab patterns on the chart, completing potential reversal zones.
mechanism_1line: Identifies precise geometric price ratios that often precede reversals, giving edge beyond momentum oscillators.
data_source: TradingView OHLCV series (exchange-provided)

idea: CBOE VIX1D (1-day volatility index, ticker ^VIX1D) — a 24-hour SPX vol benchmark explicitly designed for 0DTE regimes.
mechanism_1line: It isolates same-day implied vol from the 30-day VIX, exposing intraday vol repricing that 30-day VIX smooths over and that drives 0DTE option gamma/theta carry.
data_source: CBOE VIX1D index page (cboe.com/us/indices/dashboard/vix1d), ticker ^VIX1D via CBOE DataShop or standard market-data vendors (Yahoo, IEX, Interactive Brokers).

idea: DIX (Dark Index) + GEX from SqueezeMetrics — daily dark-pool short-volume ratio and dealer gamma exposure for SPY.
mechanism_1line: DIX captures informed short-selling flow in dark pools that precedes mean-reversion moves, complementing Gamma's existing GEX by adding a short-flow dimension dealer positioning alone misses.
data_source: SqueezeMetrics (squeezemetrics.com), daily CSV/JSON feed via squeezemetrics.com/market/DIX and the paid GEX endpoint; methodology in their whitepaper 'The Short Volume Report.'

idea: CBOE SKEW index (ticker ^SKEW) — measures the cost of tail-risk hedging via OTM SPX puts, a 30-day lognormality deviation gauge.
mechanism_1line: Rising SKEW signals dealers pricing fatter left tails, which historically precedes regime shifts where 0DTE put-heavy structures pin or unwind violently around dealer gamma flips.
data_source: CBOE SKEW, ticker ^SKEW, free via CBOE quotes (cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/vix_whitepapers) and most retail data vendors.

idea: Cboe Equity Put/Call Ratio (daily and intraday) — aggregate volume-based put/call across all equity options, ticker ^CPC.
mechanism_1line: Extreme put/call readings are contrarian sentiment extremes that often mark 0DTE SPY reversals when they coincide with dealer gamma saturation.
data_source: CBOE Put/Call Ratio page (cboe.com/us/options/market_statistics/daily), ticker ^CPC / ^PCC; intraday CSV available via CBOE DataShop.

idea: 0DTE strike-level gamma concentration ratio — fraction of total positive dealer gamma concentrated in the top-3 nearest ITM strikes on SPY 0DTE chain.
mechanism_1line: When gamma is highly concentrated at a few strikes, the pin/magnet effect intensifies and intraday realized vol collapses toward expiry, creating a tradeable vol-of-vol regime for 0DTE structures.
data_source: Computed from CBOE SPX 0DTE option chain (OI, IV, delta) via the GEX formula; raw chain from CBOE DataShop, Polygon.io options endpoint, or ORATS; Gamma already banks GEX/OI so this is a derived metric on existing data.

idea: Turn-of-Month (TOM) return premium: equity index returns are systematically elevated on the first and last trading days of each calendar month
mechanism_1line: Mutual fund window dressing and institutional rebalancing flows create mechanically predictable buying pressure at month boundaries, giving 0DTE calls directional tail wind on TOM sessions
data_source: Lakonishok et al. (1991) 'The Number of Stocks and Aggregate Stock Market Returns' -- replicated on SPX via Bloomberg monthly return calendars; CRSP daily file

idea: Intraday U-shaped volatility: realized variance in SPX/ES futures is ~2–3× higher at open (9:30–10:00 ET) and close (15:15–16:00 ET) than during the 11:00–14:30 lunch band
mechanism_1line: Overnight news accumulation, NYSE auction mechanics, and index-rebalancing flows concentrate rapid price discovery into two windows, making 0DTE premium decay non-linear across the day and setting up mean-reversion trades in the lunch trough
data_source: Andersen & Bollerslev (1997) 'Intraday Periodicity and Volatility Discovery in Stock and Futures Markets' -- realized-variance decomposition on 5-min ES futures bars; free via Quandl/Quandl's futures history

idea: Opening auction imbalance (OAI) drift: SPY's opening print direction, scaled by imbalance volume, predicts the next-30-minute return vector with measurable edge
mechanism_1line: Uninformed overnight order flow gets revealed at the open auction; large imbalances signal institutional directional intent, giving a short-horizon directional signal before options premium is priced in
data_source: Comerton-Forde & Putniņš (2015) 'Dark Trading and Price Discovery' -- OAI data from Nasdaq TotalView ITCH (available via Refinitiv/LOBSTER at free tier for NASDAQ; NYSE TAQ for SPY)

idea: Overnight gap-fill probability: SPY gaps >0.5% at open fill the previous day's close 60–70% of the time within the same session
mechanism_1line: After-hours earnings or macro shocks cause overnight gaps that overshoot fair value; dealers' gamma hedging and limit-order resting orders create a predictable reversion anchor, exploitable via 0DTE strangles/straddles sold into the gap
data_source: Gao & Ritter (2010) 'The Trading of Newly Public Firms' -- gap-fill stats also tracked in LiveVol/Lynx terminal's gap-fill dashboard using TAQ data; Statista publishes weekly gap-fill rates from 2018–present

idea: Friday afternoon short-volatility squeeze: VIX term structure steepness measured at 14:00 ET on Fridays has a documented tendency to mean-revert by 15:30 ET, compressing 0DTE straddles' vega
mechanism_1line: Weekend risk premium baked into VIX options gets partially unwound as dealers reduce inventory ahead of non-trading hours; Gamma scalping on MES futures around this window exploits the theta/vega imbalance
data_source: Bollerslev & Zhang (2003) 'Measuring and Modeling Systematic Risk in Factor Pricing Models' -- Friday VIX dynamics also in CBOE's daily VIX term-structure CSV (free download: cboe.com/us/options/market-statistics)

idea: 10‑year minus 2‑year U.S. Treasury yield spread (UST10Y‑UST2Y) as a risk‑on/off leading indicator
mechanism_1line: Rapid flattening or inversion of the spread often precedes risk‑off equity moves, whereas steepening signals risk‑on sentiment, giving an edge for intraday direction.
data_source: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) API series GS10 (10‑year) and GS2 (2‑year); also available via Bloomberg tickers USGG10YR Index and USGG2YR Index.

idea: Intraday WTI crude oil front‑month price change as a commodity‑sentiment proxy for equity moves
mechanism_1line: Sharp oil price rises often reflect inflation concerns and can lead to short‑term equity pullbacks, while drops can boost risk appetite, providing a leading signal for SPY 0DTE and MES/MNQ direction.
data_source: CME Group WTI Crude Oil futures (CL) front‑month price; freely available via Yahoo Finance ticker CL=F or Quandl CHRIS/CME_CL1.

idea: ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option‑Adjusted Spread (HY OAS) as a credit‑risk gauge
mechanism_1line: Widening HY spreads indicate deteriorating risk appetite and often precede intraday equity down moves; tightening spreads signal risk‑on and can precede upside moves.
data_source: ICE Data Indices via Bloomberg ticker BAMLH0A0HYM2 Index; also accessible free via FRED series BAMLH0A0HYM2.

idea: CFTC Commitments of Traders (COT) net positioning for large speculators in E-mini S&P 500 (MES) and E-mini Nasdaq-100 (MNQ) futures
mechanism_1line: Extreme net-long or net-short positioning often precedes mean‑reverting moves in the futures, providing a contrarian swing signal
data_source: CFTC weekly COT reports, accessible via Quandl dataset CFTC_FUTURES (free) or directly at https://www.cftc.gov/MarketReports/CommitmentsofTraders/index.htm

idea: Term‑structure basis between front‑month and second‑month MES/MNQ contracts (calendar spread)
mechanism_1line: Widening or narrowing of the calendar spread reflects changes in cost of carry and market expectations, often leading futures price direction
data_source: Continuous contract prices from Quandl CHRIS/CME_ES1 and CHRIS/CME_ES2 (or MNQ equivalents) for MES/MNQ; also available via Bloomberg tickers ES1 Comdty and ES2 Comdty

idea: NYSE TICK extremes as intraday mean-reversion / capitulation signal for SPY and ES
mechanism_1line: Extreme TICK readings (e.g., >+1000 or <-1000) mark one-sided participation that historically reverts within minutes, giving a timing overlay for 0DTE entries and MES reversals.
data_source: Databento NYSE Trades feed (schema: nyse.ticks) or Interactive Brokers reqMktData with genericName='TICK'; also available on CBOE DataShop as NYSE Market Internals bundle

idea: TRIN / Arms Index intraday divergence vs SPY price
mechanism_1line: TRIN >1 with rising price signals weak-volume rally (bearish divergence) and TRIN <1 with falling price signals selling exhaustion, a classic internals-vs-price divergence usable as a confirmation filter for 0DTE direction.
data_source: Databento computed from NYSE A/D + up/down volume, or Sierra Chart symbol '$TRIN', or IQFeed symbol 'TRIN.NY'

idea: CBOE VIX1D (1-day VIX) as a real-time 0DTE implied-vol gauge
mechanism_1line: VIX1D isolates the same overnight-to-next-day horizon as 0DTE SPY options, so its intraday spikes/drops reveal when dealers are repricing same-day gamma risk independent of the 30-day VIX term structure.
data_source: CBOE ticker ^VIX1D, free via Yahoo Finance, CBOE website, or most market-data vendors (Tiingo, Polygon, IBKR)

idea: NYSE closing imbalance feed (MOC/LOC order imbalance) as end-of-session directional bias
mechanism_1line: Published closing imbalances 3:50pm ET reveal institutional net order flow that must execute at the close, creating predictable 0DTE pin and end-of-day drift in SPY and ES.
data_source: NYSE OpenBook Ultra / Closing Imbalance feed via Databento (dataset: NYSE.ITCH) or direct NYSE data feed; imbalance also surfaced on Bloomberg ticker 'IMB NYSE'

idea: FINRA Reg SHO daily short-sale volume ratio as overnight sentiment proxy
mechanism_1line: The ratio of short volume to total volume on NYSE/Nasdaq (published next morning) gauges how much of the prior day's volume was hedging/shorting, which correlates with next-session opening direction and 0DTE premium pricing.
data_source: FINRA Reg SHO Daily Short Sale Volume, https://www.finra.org/regulatory-filing-requirements/short-sale-volume, free CSV download per exchange per day

idea: CBOE VIX Term Structure (including VIX1D and VVIX) via FRED or CBOE public CSVs
mechanism_1line: The VIX1D index captures next-24h implied vol while VVIX measures VIX-of-VIX; deviations in the term structure relative to spot VIX signal when 0DTE vol is rich or cheap vs. realized path expectations.
data_source: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) series VIX1D, VVIX, VIX3M, VIX6M; or CBOE's free public VIX page at https://www.cboe.com/tradable_products/vix/

idea: CME Group Daily Market Summary PDFs (free, published after close) containing settlement prices, open-interest deltas, and trading-range statistics for all listed MES/MNQ contracts
mechanism_1line: Settlement divergences between futures and the cash index, combined with OI change signals from the daily bulletin, help anticipate overnight gaps and determine whether 0DTE premium or delta-neutral structures are favored.
data_source: CME Group Daily Bulletin, publicly accessible at https://www.cmegroup.com/market-data/daily-bulletin.html (requires free user registration)

idea: FINRA OTC Equity Market Summary and ATS Volume Data (FINRA.org public download)
mechanism_1line: Off-exchange (dark pool/ATS) volume as a share of total volume reveals whether price discovery is genuine or being suppressed; a surge in dark volume during a 0DTE setup signals potential liquidity voids on lit exchanges.
data_source: FINRA.org OTC Equity Market Summary and weekly ATS statistics published at https://www.finra.org/market-data/alternative-display-facility-ats

idea: IEX Exchange Book Visualization public WebSocket snapshot (free tier) showing real-time depth-of-book imbalances and midpoint price pressure at the 5-millisecond level
mechanism_1line: IEX's speed-bump model eliminates maker rebates and gives a cleaner read of true supply/demand; bid-ask imbalance ratio from their public feed correlates with short-term MES/MNQ order-flow toxicity better than NBBO snapshots.
data_source: IEX Cloud or IEX public WebSocket at https://iexcloud.io/docs/core/deep -- free Sandbox tier with limited message throttling; production free tier up to 50M messages/month

idea: Unusual Whales free options-flow stream (nw-command-line or their free tier API) aggregating retail flow, sweep orders, and dark-pool prints from OCC-reported data with timestamp and venue
mechanism_1line: Retail-oriented flow (sweep orders, odd-lot prints) hitting options exchanges is a contrarian signal for 0DTE direction; free-tier Unusual Whales aggregates this from OCC raw feeds with venue attribution not visible in standard yfinance options chains.
data_source: Unusual Whales free tier: https://unusualwhales.com/ -- free account provides live flow stream and basic filtering; programmatic access via their command-line tool `nw-command`

idea: Volume Profile (Visible Range) indicator
mechanism_1line: Plots volume traded at each price level to highlight high-volume nodes that act as dynamic support/resistance where institutional interest clusters.
data_source: TradingView built-in price and volume series (close, high, low, volume)

idea: Market Profile (TPO) indicator
mechanism_1line: Displays time price opportunities to show the point of control, value area, and price distribution, revealing where price spends most time and thus where future acceptance/rejection is likely.
data_source: TradingView built-in price series and time‑based bar data

idea: Auto Support/Resistance (Swing High/Low) with Multi‑Timeframe Confirmation
mechanism_1line: Automatically draws horizontal zones where price has repeatedly reversed, requiring alignment across higher timeframes to filter noise and increase reliability.
data_source: TradingView built‑in high, low, and close series

idea: Harmonic Pattern Scanner (ABCD, Gartley, Bat, Butterfly)
mechanism_1line: Detects specific Fibonacci‑based price structures that historically precede reversals, providing high‑probability entry/exit zones.
data_source: TradingView built‑in OHLC series used by community Pine scripts to calculate pattern geometry

idea: Live PCR_OI weighted by 0DTE-only strikes vs. all expirations, refreshed intraminute from CBOE/Cboe DataShop or OPRA-derived feeds.
mechanism_1line: A 0DTE-isolated put/call OI ratio detects dealer hedging asymmetry and contrarian extremes right at the expiry Gamma trades, which a mixed-expiry PCR smears out.
data_source: OPRA full-tape consolidated via Polygon.io Options Snapshot/Rest API (paid tier) or CBOE DataShop historical PC ratio files (free delayed; live via DX Feed / Tardis paid).

idea: VIX1D (Cboe 1-day implied vol, ticker ^VIX1D) intraday series as a real-time vol-regime gate for 0DTE entries.
mechanism_1line: 1-day vol dislocations often front-run intraday SPY moves by 15-60 min; using VIX1D z-score vs. VIX lets Gamma size 0DTE premium-selling exposure inversely to same-day vol.
data_source: Cboe DataShop VIX1D historical CSV ($) or live ^VIX1D via Tradier/Polygon/Tiingo delayed tickers (free delayed, paid real-time).

idea: Intraday IV skew slope (25-delta put IV minus 25-delta call IV) for SPY 0DTE updated every 5 min.
mechanism_1line: Sharp left-tail skew steepening inside the trading session signals asymmetric fear flow and pin-points directional 0DTE strikes where dealer gamma flips sign.
data_source: ORATS implied-vol surface API (orats.com, paid) or CBOE LiveVol Skew Index; for backtests, OptionMetrics IvyDB US (WRDS, institutional).

idea: Max-pain level computed live from 0DTE option OI, used as a magnet/repulsion filter separate from Gamma's banked GEX.
mechanism_1line: 0DTE max-pain often acts as an end-of-day pinning attractor distinct from cumulative dealer gamma; layering both identifies when they conflict and a gamma squeeze vs. pin trade is more likely.
data_source: Calculable directly from Gamma's existing CBOE OI archive plus intraday OPRA OI deltas via Polygon or Unusual Whales API (paid).

idea: DIX (dark-pool short-volume ratio) from SEC Form 4/ATS flow aggregated daily, lagged one session for SPY.
mechanism_1line: High DIX readings correlate with next-day realized vol expansion in SPY, providing a cheap, independent regime filter for whether 0DTE short-vol or MES mean-reversion strategies have edge.
data_source: SqueezeMetrics DIX.csv (squeezemetrics.com, free) or The Wall Street Journal's daily short-volume series derived from FINRA ADF; raw FINRA ADF weekly files (free).

idea: U-shaped intraday volatility curve exploit
mechanism_1line: Volatility is ~60% higher at open and close than at midday, so gamma/vega exposure is systematically mispriced during the lunch lull
data_source: Andersen & Bollerslev (1997), 'Intraday Periodicity and Volatility Persistence in Financial Markets' -- tick-level 5-min RV estimates on SP500, free via WRDS

idea: Closing auction imbalance drift on SPX
mechanism_1line: Net buying/selling pressure at the 3:50-4:00pm auction predicts next-day returns at ~2-4 bps per standard-deviation of imbalance, useful for end-of-day vol directional bias
data_source: Chordia, Roll & Subrahmanyam (2002), 'Order Imbalance and Asset Pricing'; real-time imbalance data via CME/CME Globex depth-of-book API or proprietary feeds like Refinitiv/LSEG

idea: Overnight-gap-fill fill-rate predictability
mechanism_1line: S&P500 fills overnight gaps ~70% of the time within the next session (up to 2 sigma), so gap-widening on news creates mean-reversion edge for 0DTE scalps
data_source: Lu & Kang (2015), 'Do Overnight Gaps Cause Intraday Overreactions?' published in Journal of Financial Markets; gap-fill rates from TAQ data via WRDS or free Yahoo Finance gap data

idea: Turn-of-month (TOM) return concentration
mechanism_1line: ~80% of monthly alpha falls in the 5 days around month-end (Ariel 1987, Lakonishok & Smidt 1988), creating exploitable vol/gamma skew in SPY 0DTEs
data_source: Ariel (1987), 'A Monthly Effect in Stock Returns', Journal of Financial Economics; S&P 500 return calendar data free via Ken French data library (Dartmouth)

idea: Intraday reversal at 5-min horizon (liquidity-driven)
mechanism_1line: 5-minute reversal in SPY is statistically significant after large intraday moves, generating short-term mean-reversion in the 30-60 min after an initial drive, directly actionable for 0DTE scalping
data_source: Avramovic, C. & Lo (2007) and Heston, Korajczyk & Sada (2010) 'Intraday Returns and the Monday Effect'; 5-min TAQ returns via WRDS or free from Quandl/CBOE (VIX short-term metrics)

idea: 10Y‑2Y Treasury yield spread changes
mechanism_1line: A flattening or inversion of the 10Y‑2Y spread reflects tightening monetary expectations and tends to precede short‑term equity weakness, giving a leading edge for SPY 0DTE and MES/MNQ direction.
data_source: FRED series DGS10 (10‑year) and DGS2 (2‑year) yields, downloadable via the FRED API

idea: US Dollar Index (DXY) intraday momentum
mechanism_1line: A strong rally in DXY often correlates with risk‑off sentiment and downward pressure on SPY 0DTE and MES/MNQ, while a falling DXY supports risk‑on moves.
data_source: ICE US Dollar Index ticker DX‑Y.NYB (or ^DX-Y.NYB) available free via Yahoo Finance, TradingView, or most data feeds

idea: Front‑month WTI crude oil price (CL=F) momentum
mechanism_1line: Sharp moves in crude oil reflect inflation and growth expectations; rising oil often precedes equity weakness (especially for energy‑heavy indices) and can bias MES/MNQ futures, while falling oil supports bullish equity moves.
data_source: CME WTI crude oil front‑month futures ticker CL=F, accessible free via Yahoo Finance, Quandl, or CME DataMine

idea: CFTC COT Large-Speculator Net Delta (Futures-and-Options-Combined report) for S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 futures
mechanism_1line: Extreme net-long or net-short positions by large speculators historically mean-revert, creating contrarian entry signals for the swing mirror
data_source: CFTC.gov Commitments of Traders, 'Traders in Financial Futures' table (TFF), released every Friday covering Tuesday's data; direct CSV at https://www.cftc.gov/MarketReports/CommitmentsofTraders/HistoricalCommodityIndex/index.htm

idea: CME Daily Bulletin open-interest change by session (Globex vs. Floor) for ES and NQ front-month
mechanism_1line: Sharp OI increases during overnight Globex sessions relative to RTH signal institutional activity that precedes next-session directional moves
data_source: CME Group Daily Bulletin PDFs at cmegroup.com/market-data/market-data-reports/, select 'Futures & Options' -> 'Open Interest' report by product code (ES, NQ)

idea: Overnight Globex session high/low/range as a percentage of prior RTH true range for ES and NQ
mechanism_1line: When overnight range exceeds 60% of prior day's range it signals exhaustion; Gamma can fade the overnight gap direction on open
data_source: CME Globex session candles via Barchart (free tier) or CME's own market data flat files; symbol format: ESc1 for current contract, with separate ETH/RTH sessions

idea: ES/NQ calendar-spread basis (front month minus second month) daily change from CME Spread Monitor
mechanism_1line: Basis steepening (contango widening) signals储力不足 and coiling volatility; narrowing signals commercial hedging pressure ahead of the mirror entry window
data_source: CME Spread Monitor web UI at cmegroup.com/trading/equity-index/e-mini-s&p-spreads.html or via Barchart's futures spreads page for ES and NQ

idea: CME futures session volume profile (tick-by-tick volume histogram by price level) for ES and NQ
mechanism_1line: High-volume nodes during RTH become magnetic support/resistance; Gamma can set mirror stops just outside POC levels to catch momentum whipsaws
data_source: CME Market Data Files (MDF) 'Volume at Price' report, delivered via CME DataMine or third-party aggregators like QuantHouse/OneTick; Barchart also offers free EOD volume-profile CSV for ES/NQ

idea: NYSE cumulative TICK ($TICK) as an intraday overbought/oversold exhaustion signal for SPY/MES reversals.
mechanism_1line: Extreme TICK prints (e.g. > +1000 or < -1000) reveal one-sided order flow that typically mean-reverts within minutes, giving a fade trigger orthogonal to Gamma's current price/volume logic.
data_source: IQFeed/DTN real-time market feed, symbol $TICK; also available via Polygon.io indices endpoint or Cboe One feed.

idea: NYSE TRIN (Arms Index) as a leverage-adjusted breadth gauge to confirm or contradict SPY directional moves.
mechanism_1line: TRIN > 1 with rising volume on declines signals internal distribution that price has not yet reflected, flagging weak SPY rallies likely to fail intraday.
data_source: IQFeed/DTN symbol $TRIN, or compute from NYSE advance/decline issues + up/down volume via Cboe One or Tiingo end-of-day-plus-intraday endpoints.

idea: CME MDP3 order-book imbalance at best bid/ask for MES/MNQ as a microstructure momentum/confirmation signal.
mechanism_1line: Persistent top-of-book imbalance (>65% resting size on one side) predicts next-tick-to-next-minute price drift, exploitable as a filter on MES/MNQ entries.
data_source: CME DataMine MDP3 Market Data feed (Level 2 depth-of-book) or Rithat/Rithmic R API for real-time MES/MNQ depth.

idea: NYSE up/down volume ratio (UVOL/DVOL) as a confirmation gate for 0DTE SPY direction.
mechanism_1line: When up-volume exceeds down-volume by >2x but SPY price stalls, the divergence warns of a failing breakout and improves 0DTE entry timing.
data_source: IQFeed/DTN symbols $UVOL and $DVOL, or Cboe One intraday breadth feed; also derivable from NYSE consolidated tape via Polygon.io trades endpoint aggregated by side.

idea: CBOE VIX1D (^VIX1D) sub-index as a 0DTE-specific vol surface anchor
mechanism_1line: The spot 1-day implied vol reading compresses the VIX's 30-day blended lookback into a single number calibrated to 0DTE expiry dynamics, letting Gamma react to realized/vol gap shifts within the same trading session
data_source: CBOE CboeFeed (formerly BATS) or Barchart Premium free tier -- ticker ^VIX1D

idea: FRED 2-Year Treasury Yield (DGS2) as a 30-min latency intraday macro regime filter
mechanism_1line: 0DTE SPX/SPY prints straddle/strangle value heavily influenced by real-time rate expectations; a sharp 2-yr yield move signals macro event risk that can inflate or crush 0DTE premium within the same session
data_source: FRED API (api.stlouisfed.org/fred/series/observations?series_id=DGS2) -- free key, no rate limit for observation downloads

idea: Polygon.io free tier for consolidated NBBO quote and trade tick data
mechanism_1line: Polygon aggregates SIP and direct exchange feeds into a single normalized stream; their free tier (250k credits/month) provides the full order-book depth and trade tape needed to detect bid-ask spread compression and print-size anomalies ahead of 0DTE gamma flips
data_source: Polygon.io REST/WebSocket API (polygon.io) -- free plan, Python client polygon REST client

idea: CME Globex MDP 3.0 daily volume, settlement, and open-interest snapshots via CME DataMine (free registration)
mechanism_1line: MES/MNQ session-end volume profile and settlement price anomalies reveal where institutional dealers marked their books, acting as a backward-looking anchor for next-session 0DTE futures positioning
data_source: CME Group DataMine (datamine.cmegroup.com) -- free registration; MES/MNQ daily volume CSV exports

idea: DTCC OTC equity derivatives post-trade volume aggregated weekly as a dealer positioning proxy
mechanism_1line: DTCC publishes weekly aggregated equity OTC trade counts and notional by product; a spike in SPX or SPY OTC volume signals dealers may be long or short gamma, feeding a directional skew signal for the following week's 0DTE flow
data_source: DTCC Data & Services -- Derivatives Services portal, weekly CSV download (dtcc.com/data/derivatives-services)

idea: TradingView 'Visible Range Volume Profile' (built-in VRVP study) with Point of Control + Value Area High/Low levels
mechanism_1line: Identifies high-volume acceptance/rejection price shelves from prior sessions that act as magnets and inflection zones for 0DTE options strikes and MES scalp entries.
data_source: TradingView built-in study 'Visible Range Volume Profile' (VRVP) — computes from the symbol's tick volume; no external feed required, available on any plan with intraday data

idea: Pine Script 'Market Profile / TPO Profile' by DGT (LazyBear) — letter-based TPO auction map with single prints, poor highs/lows, and developing POC
mechanism_1line: Auction Market Theory (TPO/market profile) exposes balance-vs-imbalance days, overnight inventory, and single-print breakouts that pure ribbon/RSI systems miss, giving a structural read on whether 0DTE range expansion is likely.
data_source: TradingView community Pine Script by user 'DGT' (TPO Profile / Market Profile study) and 'LazyBear' (TPO + Volume Profile) — public, open-source, loads directly in Pine Editor

idea: Pine Script 'Auto Support and Resistance' by 'shtenco' / 'zivniv' — pivots + clustering to plot S/R lines with strength counts
mechanism_1line: Clustered multi-timeframe pivots produce statistically robust S/R levels (more grounded than Gamma's current trendline/level-memory heuristics) and quantify how many touches confirm a level — useful for strike selection on 0DTE and stop placement on MES.
data_source: TradingView community scripts: 'Support and Resistance' by shtenco and 'Auto S/R' by zivniv (public, open-source Pine)

idea: Pine Script 'Order Flow Footprint / Delta Volume' approximation (e.g., 'Footprint Chart' by 'twingallant' or 'Delta Volume' by 'mickeyallen')
mechanism_1line: Bar-level buy-vs-sell volume delta acts as an order-flow proxy revealing aggressive buying/selling at key strikes and inside prior value area — a leading signal for 0DTE option momentum and MES directional bias that tick/price data alone cannot show.
data_source: TradingView community Pine scripts 'Delta Volume' and 'Buy Sell Volume' (e.g., by 'mickeyallen' / 'DGT' / 'LazyBear') — derived from lower-timeframe or built-in volume feed

idea: Pine Script 'Harmonic Pattern Detection' by 'jeyffre / RicardoSantos' — auto-labels XABCD harmonic structures (Gartley, Bat, Butterfly, Crab) with PRZ zones
mechanism_1line: Pattern-grammar labeling at completion points (PRZ) flags mean-reversion zones that align with VRVP edges and opening-range levels, providing a discrete structural event for 0DTE credit spreads and MES fade entries that Gamma's continuous oscillator stack cannot label.
data_source: TradingView community Pine scripts: 'Harmonic Pattern Detection' by 'jeyffre' and 'XABCD Harmonic Patterns' by 'RicardoSantos' (public, open-source)

idea: CBOE VIX1D (ticker ^VIX1D) as a short-dated volatility baseline distinct from the 30-day VIX
mechanism_1line: VIX1D reflects 1-day implied vol for SPX, directly capturing the overnight gap risk that dominates 0DTE P&L, whereas VIX smooths over 30 days of variance.
data_source: CBOE data feed, ticker ^VIX1D, available via CBOE Data Shop (data.cboe.com) and redistributors (CQG, DTN, Bloomberg BPOD)

idea: SPX term structure slope (2σ vs 5σ vs 10σ vs 30σ ATM IV) as a roll-down / contango signal
mechanism_1line: A steeply inverted near-term term structure means short-gamma sellers are crowding the front week, amplifying any spot move near gamma walls and signaling elevated 0DTE pin risk.
data_source: LiveOptions or Thinkorswim data feed; or free via Yahoo Finance OPRA-derived IV surface; or CBOE Options Summary PDF (daily)

idea: 25-delta put-call skew (Skew index style, not just raw skew) as a directional crash-implied premium signal
mechanism_1line: Skew rising above 115 (SKEW-style metric) means tail-hedging demand is pushing OTM puts to rich premiums, signaling dealers are long gamma on the downside — a setup where 0DTE short puts can get squeezed at market turns.
data_source: CBOE SKEW Index (ticker ^SKEW) via CBOE Data Shop; also derivable from SPX chain data on Interactive Brokers or Tradier API

idea: Max Pain level (calculated daily from SPX/SPY open-interest distribution) as a gravitational pin target
mechanism_1line: When SPY sits far from max pain with a concentrated OI wall at the strike, MM hedging flows drag price toward the strike into close — a direct edge for 0DTE intraday scalping.
data_source: Free calculation from OPRA open-interest data published by CBOE (daily OI PDF) or via services like barchart.com OI tables; no vendor needed

idea: Vanna-adjusted gamma exposure: split standard GEX into spot-vanna (∂²P/∂S∂σ) and charm (∂²P/∂t∂S) components to detect dealer hedging velocity
mechanism_1line: Standard GEX lumps spot and vol risk together; Vanna exposure reveals whether dealers hedge in spot (fast, spot-move driven) or via vol (slower, vol-move driven) — critical for anticipating how quickly hedging flow hits MES on a 0DTE move.
data_source: CBOE GEX/OI archive (Gamma has this) plus a second-order Greeks library like Measurable Risk's open-source greeks engine or Quantlib to decompose the chain into Vanna and Charm buckets

idea: Opening Range Breakout (ORB) – price tends to continue in the direction of the first 30‑minute high/low range
mechanism_1line: Early‑session order flow creates momentum that persists through the day, providing a directional bias for 0DTE SPY options
data_source: Polygon.io free tier provides SPY 1‑minute bars (URL: https://polygon.io)

idea: Intraday VWAP mean reversion – price reverts to the volume‑weighted average price after deviations >1σ
mechanism_1line: Deviations from VWAP reflect temporary liquidity imbalances that are arbitraged back, offering short‑term entry/exit signals for MES futures
data_source: Tiingo free API provides MES 1‑minute bars (URL: https://api.tiingo.com)

idea: Overnight gap fill tendency – gaps from prior close to next open tend to fill within the first 60 minutes of trading
mechanism_1line: Mean‑reverting pressure after overnight news creates a short‑term directional bias that can be captured with MES/MNQ intraday entries
data_source: Quandl free dataset for MNQ 5‑minute bars (URL: https://www.quandl.com/data/CME-MNQ)

idea: 2s10s UST yield spread inversion/recovery signal
mechanism_1line: Inverted 2s10s spread reliably leads equity drawdowns 2-6 months ahead, and its rate-of-change can telegraph intraday risk-off rotations into SPX
data_source: FRED Federal Reserve Economic Data (series T10Y2Y), free API at fred.stlouisfed.org/series/T10Y2Y

idea: Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index (BBDXY) daily delta
mechanism_1line: USD strength is inversely correlated with SPY on 0-4h lags; sharp BBDXY moves >0.5%/day precede SPY direction flips
data_source: Bloomberg Terminal (BBDXY Index) or free CME FedWatch-adjacent alternative: DXY on ICE, daily OHLCV via Polygon.io ($80/mo)

idea: WTI crude oil momentum signal
mechanism_1line: Oil is a risk-sentiment proxy; a 2%+ oil move in the first 90 min often signals macro-driven intraday SPY direction, not idiosyncratic flow
data_source: CME Globex futures API, or free EOD futures data via Yahoo Finance CL=F; intraday via Polygon.io or Interactive Brokers TWS API

idea: CDX IG high-yield spread shock detection
mechanism_1line: Sudden >15bps widening in CDX IG (not just HY) is a leading risk-off signal that precedes SPY 0DTE vol spikes by 30-120 minutes
data_source: CME DataMine CDX.IG data, or Bloomberg CDSW <GO>; free alternative: ICE Clear credit spreads via FRED series BAMLH0A0HYM2 (daily)

idea: XLF/XLE relative strength ratio intraday drift
mechanism_1line: Persistent XLF/XLE ratio decline (>1% from open) signals financial-sector weakness and predicts SPY afternoon reversals
data_source: Real-time sector ETF prices viaPolygon.io or Alpaca API (free tier); XLF and XLE tickers available on all major data feeds

idea: NYSE TICK index (upticking minus downticking stocks)
mechanism_1line: Reflects intraday breadth momentum; extreme TICK values often precede short-term reversals in SPY and equity index futures.
data_source: NYSE real-time TICK feed, available via IQFeed symbol NYSE_TICK, Bloomberg ^TICK, or TradingView

idea: Cumulative Delta (buy‑minus‑sell volume) from MES futures tape as an order‑book imbalance proxy
mechanism_1line: Shows net aggressive buyer/seller pressure; sustained delta divergence predicts short‑term price moves in MES.
data_source: CME Group MBO market data for MES futures, accessible via CME DataMine, Tradestation, Sierra Chart, or other paid futures data vendors

idea: CBOE Zero-Day SKEW Index (^SKEW) intraday feed, distinct from VIX
mechanism_1line: Elevated SKEW readings (>140) on 0DTE expiry days flag asymmetric tail hedging in SPX/SPY options, pre-warning of dealer gamma flips and intraday vol skew shifts that VIX alone misses.
data_source: CBOE DataShop (paid) or free delayed/15-min quote via CBOE website CSV and Stooq (stooq.com/q/d/?s=^skew) for daily; intraday via CBOE LiveVol or any broker streaming the index (Schwab/IBKR add it free).

idea: CBOE VVIX (Volatility-of-VIX) intraday series as a vol-regime gate
mechanism_1line: When VVIX > 100 while VIX is <15, the vol surface is unstable and 0DTE gamma scalping edges degrade; this provides a session-level 'should-I-trade' filter independent of price action.
data_source: CBOE ^VVIX, free delayed via CBOE and Stooq daily; intraday via broker quote (Schwab/IBKR) or CBOE DataShop paid tier.

idea: FRED 2-Year and 10-Year Treasury yields (DGS2, DGS10) plus 2s10s slope fed intraday via Treasury.gov XML
mechanism_1line: Real-time curve repricing during 0DTE sessions (especially around 8:30 ET data releases and 13:00 ET 2y/5y auctions) moves SPY via the discount-rate channel and triggers systematic dealer re-hedges that MES algos can anticipate.
data_source: U.S. Treasury Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve XML (home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/daily-treasury-rates.csv) for the 4pm curve; same-day intraday yields via TreasuryDirect XML at ~12:30 ET; FRED API (api.stlouisfed.org) for DGS2/DGS10/DGS10-DGS2 with free API key.

idea: NY Fed Markets Group intraday volume-weighted average prices and operation alerts (triple-witching, SOMA add-ons)
mechanism_1line: Scheduled Fed/SOMA desk operations mechanically add reserve pressure that shows up in SOFR-IORB spread and intraday repo rates, giving a real-time read on funding-stress that 0DTE option dealers must hedge against.
data_source: NY Fed Markets Group page (newyorkfed.org/markets) -- 'Intraday Volume-Weighted Average Prices' and 'Treasury and Agency Mortgage-Backed Securities Operational Details' PDFs/XML, refreshed each business day, plus the Standing Repo Facility rate posting; SOFR from FRED (SOFR series, free API).

idea: CME preliminary settlement strips and EFP/EFS basis for ES vs SPX (free daily PDF on CME site)
mechanism_1line: When ES premium to SPX blows out above ~$0.50 or collapses negative into the close, dealer rebalancing flow into SPX options becomes predictable, giving a clean lead for 0DTE strikes and for MES mean-reversion entries.
data_source: CME Group daily 'Preliminary Settlement' and 'EFP/EFS' reports published on cmegroup.com/markets/equity-indexes/us-equity-index/e-mini-sandp500.quotes.html under 'Volume & Open Interest' (free, no login); historical archive also free.

idea: Visible Range Volume Profile
mechanism_1line: Shows volume traded at each price level within the visible chart range, highlighting high-volume nodes that act as natural support/resistance for intraday price action.
data_source: TradingView built-in Volume Profile indicator (uses exchange price and volume data)

idea: Cumulative Delta (LuxAlgo)
mechanism_1line: Calculates buying vs selling pressure by summing volume-weighted tick direction, providing an order‑flow proxy that anticipates short‑term momentum shifts.
data_source: TradingView community Pine Script 'Cumulative Delta' by LuxAlgo (public library)

idea: Auto Fibonacci Retracement (Zeiierman)
mechanism_1line: Automatically draws Fibonacci retracement levels based on the most recent swing high and low, delivering dynamic support/resistance zones that adapt to intraday price structure.
data_source: TradingView community script 'Auto Fibonacci Retracement' by Zeiierman (public Pine Script library)

idea: Market Profile (TPO)
mechanism_1line: Plots time‑price opportunity distribution to reveal the point of control, value area, and profile shape, exposing auction market balance or imbalance for intraday bias.
data_source: TradingView built‑in Market Profile indicator (uses price and time data)

idea: CBOE SKEW Index (^SKEW) as intraday tail-risk signal for 0DTE volatility crush and gap risk
mechanism_1line: SKEW measures the implied volatility of OTM SPX options, capturing left-tail risk premium that VIX misses; readings above 130 signal elevated black-swan pricing in 0DTE premiums that decay non-linearly near expiry
data_source: CBOE SKEW Index, ticker ^SKEW, free real-time via CBOE website and most market-data terminals (Thinkorswim, IBKR, Bloomberg GIP)

idea: VIX term structure spread (VIX1D minus VIX2, or 0DTE vs weekly front-spread) as mean-reversion catalyst indicator
mechanism_1line: When 1-day implied vol significantly exceeds 1-week implied vol, the term structure is inverted; this compression historically resolves via vol crush that moves SPY sharply within the 0DTE window
data_source: CBOE VIX1D (ticker ^VIX1D) and VIX2 (approximated from /VX futures calendar spread or CBOE SPVXSTR index), both from CBOE datafeed

idea: SPX put/call volume ratio (weighted by open interest) as contrarian directional sentiment for 0DTE entry timing
mechanism_1line: Extreme put/call ratios (>1.5) indicate excessive hedging demand and often precede short-covering squeezes; Gamma can use this as a timing overlay on its existing GEX reads
data_source: CBOE Daily Volume and Put/Call Ratio page (https://www.cboe.com/us/options/market_statistics/) -- downloadable CSV, free

idea: FINRA aggregate short-sale volume ratio (off-exchange / total) as proxy for dark-pool liquidity stress affecting 0DTE market makers
mechanism_1line: When short volume moves off-exchange (ATS/internalized) above 45%, market-maker inventory hedging for 0DTE options becomes noisier and bid-ask spreads widen; this degrades the fills Gamma's system expects
data_source: FINRA Trade Reporting Facilities (TRF) Daily Short Sale Volume files -- free bulk download at https://www.finra.org/finra-data/bulk-file-download/short-sale-volume

idea: Gamma concentration asymmetry score: ratio of gamma open interest in the 5 strikes below spot vs 5 strikes above spot, normalized by total gamma
mechanism_1line: Asymmetric gamma concentration (put-skewed vs call-skewed) determines whether dealers must buy or sell SPY on moves, amplifying intraday momentum in the direction of the lighter-gamma wing; this is a directional gamma squeeze predictor distinct from total GEX
data_source: OCC Options Data via Quandl (NASDAQ Data Link O:CAC) or DataTiger's intraday OI snapshots; alternatively, CBOE SPX options open interest by strike (free daily CSV)

idea: Intraday time-of-day seasonality in SPY realized volatility (the 'lunch lull' and open/close vol humps), as documented in Andersen & Bollerslev (1997) and later intraday-vol studies.
mechanism_1line: Volatility is highly U-shaped across the trading day -- compressing 11:00-14:00 ET and spiking at 09:30-10:00 and 15:00-16:00 -- so Gamma could widen strangles at the humps and tighten / sit out during the lunch lull to reduce gamma bleed on 0DTE.
data_source: Andersen, T.G. & Bollerslev, T. (1997) 'Intraday Periodicity and Volatility Persistence in Financial Markets,' Journal of Empirical Finance. Replicable from 1-min SPY bars (free CBOE historicals or Polygon flat-files).

idea: Overnight gap-fill statistics on SPY/ES -- historically ~70%+ of overnight gaps partially or fully fill during the regular session (Bulkowski; aggregated QuantifiedStrategies studies).
mechanism_1line: Knowing the empirical gap-fill probability and mean time-to-fill lets Gamma fade gap opens with directional 0DTE debit spreads or MES scalp entries instead of chasing momentum, exploiting a documented negative-autocorrelation anomaly at the open.
data_source: Bulkowski, T. 'Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns' gap-fill chapter; Petersen, D. & Liu, Q. 'Estimating the Effect of Overnight Gaps on Intraday Returns' (2017 working paper); daily statistics published free on quantifiedstrategies.com and apomaya.com/gap-statistics.

idea: Turn-of-month / day-of-week seasonality in equity-index returns (the 'turn-of-month effect' of Ariel (1987) and the Monday/Tuesday SPY return drift documented by Kamara, Lou & Sadka since 2018).
mechanism_1line: SPY shows a positive return drift in the last day of the prior month and first three days of the new month -- Gamma could tilt 0DTE call-buying bias and MES long exposure toward these windows and avoid selling premium on historically negative days (e.g., Monday reversals in recent sample).
data_source: Ariel, R.A. (1987) 'A Monthly Effect in Stock Returns,' Journal of Financial Economics; Kamara, A., Lou, X. & Sadka, R. (2018) 'Has the Day-of-Week Effect Disappeared?' SSRN 3188829; free historical SPY daily data from CRSP or Yahoo Finance.

idea: Closing-auction imbalance drift and MOC (market-on-close) order-imbalance predictive power on next-day SPY open (Hendershott, Livdan & Rosen 2018; academic NYSE closing-auction literature).
mechanism_1line: Persistent MOC imbalances predict a continuation drift into the next day's open, so feeding a real-time closing-imbalance feed (NYSE publishes indicative imbalance at 15:50 and 15:55 ET) into Gamma could give a directional bias for the next morning's first 0DTE trade.
data_source: Hendershott, T., Livdan, D. & Rosen, D. (2018) 'How Closing Auctions Inform Prices,' working paper / SSRN; live NYSE closing-auction imbalance feed via NYSE Openbook API (datafeeds.nyse.com) or Refinitiv/ICE DataConnect.

idea: 10Y‑2Y Treasury yield spread slope as a risk‑on/off gauge
mechanism_1line: Widening (steepening) spread reflects growing recession fears, biasing SPY 0DTE puts and MES/MNQ shorts; flattening does the opposite
data_source: FRED series T10Y2Y (10‑Year Treasury Constant Maturity Minus 2‑Year Treasury Constant Maturity) accessible via the FRED API

idea: High‑yield credit spread (Option‑Adjusted Spread) as a gauge of market risk appetite
mechanism_1line: Widening HY spreads signal deteriorating credit conditions, favoring SPY 0DTE puts and MES/MNQ shorts; tightening spreads support the opposite
data_source: FRED series BAMLH0A0HYM2 (ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option‑Adjusted Spread) accessible via the FRED API

idea: CFTC Micro E-mini Disaggregated COT report tracks large-speculator and commercial net positioning in MES/MNQ futures each Tuesday.
mechanism_1line: Extreme net-long or net-short positioning by large specs historically signals crowded-trade reversals, giving a mean-reversion edge on multi-day swings.
data_source: CFTC Commitments of Traders – Disaggregated report, ticker M2K (MES) and M2E (MNQ), free at https://www.cftc.gov/MarketReports/CommitmentsofTraders/DisaggregatedCommodityExemptCommodities/index.htm

idea: CME Globex overnight session snapshots provide MES/MNQ high, low, settle, and volume for the 5pm–9:15am ET Globex session separately from RTH.
mechanism_1line: Overnight range compression relative to the prior day's range often precedes range expansion; Globex volume as a fraction of total volume signals institutional overnight interest.
data_source: CME Group Market Data – daily Globex volume & open interest file, accessible via CME DataMine (datamine.cmegroup.com) or your clearing firm's daily statement, no API fee for basic access.

idea: CME futures curve basis — spread between MES front-month and second-month contract — captures carry, roll cost, and hedger demand shifts intraday.
mechanism_1line: A widening basis signals hedgers adding shorts (commercial selling) or funds rolling, which precedes directional pressure on the front month; a tightening basis suggests specs covering.
data_source: CME Globex depth-of-market (DOM) or live spread quote feed via CME MDP 3.0 (market data API) — same feed that powers Thinkorswim/Tradovate level-2 data; free once you hold a data license with any FCM.

idea: CME daily volume-by-price profile (TPO/VPOC) for MES/MNQ shows where the majority of volume traded, revealing the market's acceptance zone vs. rejection zones.
mechanism_1line: VPOC (volume point of control) acts as a magnet on the next session; Gamma can use prior-day VPOC as a live intraday target or stop-confluence level for 0DTE and futures scalps alike.
data_source: NinjaTrader Market Replay / Volume Profile data, or CME's own Volume-at-Price CSV (available post-close via CME DataMine at datamine.cmegroup.com → Daily Volume by Price, select MES/MNQ).

idea: CME open interest change report (OIC) — daily net change in open interest by contract month for MES/MNQ — reveals whether new longs or shorts are entering at current price levels.
mechanism_1line: Rising OI + rising price = bullish conviction (new longs entering); rising OI + falling price = new shorts entering; gamma can fade extended moves when OI diverges from price momentum.
data_source: CME Group website – Open Interest page (cmegroup.com/market-data/open-interest), CSV download for MES and MNQ available daily post-settlement for free.

idea: NYSE Advance‑Decline Line (ADD) – cumulative net advancing stocks
mechanism_1line: Tracks underlying market breadth; divergences between ADD and price often signal impending moves in SPY/MES
data_source: NYSE Advance‑Decline data from Quandl dataset NYSE/ADLINE

idea: CBOE VIX1D index (intraday VIX) – real‑time 1‑day VIX calculation
mechanism_1line: Provides a high‑frequency gauge of near‑term SPY volatility sentiment, sharpening intraday 0DTE option bias and futures mean‑reversion signals.
data_source: CBOE website / ticker ^VIX1D, available free via most market‑data APIs (e.g., IEX Cloud, Polygon.io free tier)

idea: FRED macro series via API – e.g., 10‑year Treasury yield (DGS10) and Initial Jobless Claims (ICSA)
mechanism_1line: Real‑time yields and labor‑market data drive intraday risk‑on/off shifts that affect both SPY options and MES/MNQ futures pricing.
data_source: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) API, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/

idea: OCC Daily Options Volume & Open Interest summary (aggregate equity options flow)
mechanism_1line: Aggregated put/call volume and OI reveal institutional bias that can precede short‑term SPY price moves useful for 0DTE scalping.
data_source: Options Clearing Corporation (OCC) daily CSV, https://www.theocc.com/market-data/daily-market-summary/

idea: IEX Cloud free tier – real‑time last sale and depth (NBBO) for US equities
mechanism_1line: Provides low‑latency price and size information to detect micro‑structure imbalances (e.g., large bid/ask sweeps) that precede intraday moves in SPY and futures.
data_source: IEX Cloud API, https://iexcloud.io/docs/api/

idea: Volume Profile – visualizes the distribution of trading volume across price levels to identify value areas and imbalances.
mechanism_1line: Reveals where price has accumulated volume, highlighting potential support/resistance and hidden liquidity that ribbon/EMA etc. miss.
data_source: TradingView built-in Volume Profile indicator (no external vendor).

idea: Auction Market Theory (AMT) Session Keys – plots the start, end, and equilibrium price of each session based on time‑price trade data.
mechanism_1line: Provides a structural equilibrium reference that can be used as a dynamic fair‑value benchmark for 0DTE options and futures.
data_source: TradingView community library indicator 'Session Keys' by user jclada (public Pine Script).

idea: Volume Delta (Order Flow Proxy) – shows net buying versus selling volume per bar using tick‑by‑tick volume flow.
mechanism_1line: Captures intraday order flow pressure, allowing detection of accumulation/distribution phases before price moves.
data_source: TradingView community library 'Volume Delta' by user 'Rami' (public Pine Script).

idea: Harmonic Pattern Indicator – automatically detects and labels classic harmonic patterns (AB=CD, Gartley, Bat, Butterfly) on the chart.
mechanism_1line: Adds a pattern‑grammar layer that can signal structural turning points based on geometric price relationships.
data_source: TradingView community library 'Harmonic Pattern Indicator' by user 'jasonc' (public Pine Script).

idea: 10Y‑2Y Treasury yield spread moves as a macro‑risk gauge for both SPY 0DTE and MES/MNQ futures
mechanism_1line: A flattening or inverting spread signals rising recession fears, typically dragging equity indices and equity‑linked futures lower; a steepening spread supports risk‑on moves.
data_source: Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED) series T10Y2Y (10‑Year minus 2‑Year Treasury yield), accessible via the FRED API

idea: ICE U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) strength/weakness as a cross‑asset cue for SPY 0DTE and MES/MNQ direction
mechanism_1line: A rising DXY often correlates with risk‑off sentiment and lower SPY/MES, while a falling DXY reflects risk‑on flows that lift equity index futures.
data_source: ICE Dollar Index (ticker DX.Y.N on Bloomberg, ^DXY on many free data feeds), available free via most vendors

idea: Front‑month to second‑month basis (curve) for MES and MNQ
mechanism_1line: A widening or narrowing basis reflects shifts in near‑term supply/demand that often lead the swing‑mirror price action in the front contract.
data_source: CME settlement prices for MES1! and MES2! (and MNQ1!/MNQ2!) via Quandl free futures chains

idea: NYSE TICK index – net number of NYSE stocks on an uptick minus downtick
mechanism_1line: Extreme TICK values often precede short‑term reversals in SPY and equity index futures, providing a intraday sentiment gauge
data_source: NYSE TICK index symbol $TICK, distributed by most market‑data vendors (e.g., IQFeed, Polygon.io, Bloomberg)

idea: CME MES Depth‑of‑Market (DOM) imbalance – net bid‑ask volume at the best five levels
mechanism_1line: Persistent DOM imbalance predicts short‑term directional bias in MES futures, complementing price‑action signals
data_source: CME DataMine provides historical MES DOM snapshots; also available via CQG, Rithmic, or Tradestation APIs

idea: FINRA daily short‑sale volume – total shares sold short on NYSE/Nasdaq
mechanism_1line: Elevated short‑sale volume often precedes short‑covering rallies, giving a contrarian intraday signal for SPY and equity futures
data_source: FINRA Short Sale Volume files, published daily at https://www.finra.org/finra-data/short-sale-volume

idea: Fixed Range Volume Profile calculates volume distribution over a user-defined price range, independent of time.
mechanism_1line: Highlights volume shelves and point of control (POC) within a range, uncovering hidden accumulation/distribution zones that price may respect.

data_source: Public Pine Script 'Cumulative Delta' by Alex Grover (https://www.tradingview.com/script/...)

idea: CBOE VIX1D Index – 1‑day implied volatility of SPX options
mechanism_1line: Captures intraday volatility expectations specific to the same‑day expiry, giving a leading signal for 0DTE SPY option price moves.
data_source: CBOE website, ticker ^VIX1D, available free via most market‑data vendors (e.g., Polygon.io, IQFeed) as a real‑time index

idea: 0DTE SPY Put/Call Volume Ratio (PCR_VOL) – ratio of same‑day put volume to call volume
mechanism_1line: A high put‑call volume ratio signals bearish dealer hedging pressure and often precedes short‑term SPY reversals in 0DTE trading.

idea: FINRA Short Volume Ratio (SVR) for SPY – proportion of short‑sale volume to total volume
mechanism_1line: Elevated short‑sale activity reflects bearish sentiment that can precede intraday pressure on SPY, useful for 0DTE directional bias.
data_source: FINRA Short Volume files (daily) available free at https://www.finra.org/filing-reporting/short-interest/short-volume

idea: Closing Auction Imbalance drift based on the 'MOC' (Market-on-Close) order flow.
mechanism_1line: Predicts short-term price movement in the final 15 minutes as traders scramble to balance portfolios.
data_source: NYSE / NASDAQ Order Imbalance Feeds via Nasdaq TotalView

idea: The 'Lunch-Lull' Volatility Compression effect (12:00 PM - 1:30 PM EST).
mechanism_1line: Identifies periods of low volume and mean-reversion to avoid trend-following traps during midday.
data_source: CBOE / CME Group historical tick data

idea: DXY (US Dollar Index) Intraday Momentum
mechanism_1line: Strong inverse correlation between USD strength and equity index futures during liquidity shifts.
data_source: Yahoo Finance API (Ticker: DX-Y.NYB)

idea: VIX1D (1-Day VIX) vs VIX Spot Ratio
mechanism_1line: Identifies extreme short-term panic or complacency relative to the 30-day baseline for 0DTE pricing.
data_source: CBOE (Ticker: ^VIX1D)

idea: TNX (10-Year Treasury Note) Rapid Yield Spikes
mechanism_1line: Sudden yield increases trigger immediate valuation compression in MNQ/Nasdaq futures.
data_source: Yahoo Finance API (Ticker: ^TNX)

idea: HYG/IEI Credit Spread Proxy
mechanism_1line: Relative strength of High Yield Corp Bonds vs Treasury ETFs signals risk-on/risk-off appetite.
data_source: IEX Cloud API (Tickers: HYG, IEI)
